findings.summary: "a per-stream lease read would give 12" is false -- MEASURED 6. The same wrong number is repeated at :76, SPEC.md:305 and backlog.md:42
findings.detail: I reinstated the exact mutation the diff names -- scaling ONLY the lease read per RunKey in RemoteSequencer.commitAll -- and ran :sequencer:test. The new test reds at the four-stream assertion with `expected: 3L but was: 6L`. Six, not twelve: four per-RunKey lease GETs plus the election's one STAT and one GET. Twelve is the count for a DIFFERENT shape, all three requests scaling per stream, which is not the mutation any of the four sites names. Sites: FleetSequencerCostTest.java:97 (the AssertJ `.as(...)` description, which is what an engineer reads when the assertion reds), FleetSequencerCostTest.java:76 ("per-stream scaling gives 3 and 12"), SPEC.md:305 ("it now gives 3 and 12 and reds" -- asserted as MEASURED), backlog.md:42 ("At four they are 3 and 12"). Failure scenario: M5.6g, or any later change, regresses the lease read to per-RunKey. The test reds with 6. The engineer reads the assertion message saying a per-stream lease read gives 12, concludes 6 is not that shape, and hunts a different cause -- in the one assertion this project has that enforces non-negotiable 6 on the commit path. Worse for a COST task: SPEC.md:305 is the authoritative cost cell and it now states a measured figure that is wrong by 2x, in the same cell the task exists to make correct. Either state 6 (the mutation named), or name the all-three-per-stream shape that actually gives 12 and measure that one.
findings.failure_scenario: M5.6g, or any later change, regresses the lease read to per-RunKey. The test reds at four streams with 6. The engineer reads the assertion's own message -- "a per-stream lease read would give 12" -- concludes 6 is some other shape, and hunts a different cause, in the one assertion the tree has enforcing non-negotiable 6 on the commit path. Meanwhile SPEC.md:305, the authoritative cost cell, states a MEASURED figure that is wrong by 2x in the cell this task exists to make correct.

findings.summary: The cost row and the backlog cell both name the pin as `FleetSequencerTest.aForwardedCommitCostsTHREEReadsAtANYNumberOfStreams`; that method is not in FleetSequencerTest -- it is in the new FleetSequencerCostTest
findings.detail: Verified by grep over the whole tree: `aForwardedCommitCostsTHREEReadsAtANYNumberOfStreams` occurs exactly once in source, at FleetSequencerCostTest.java:88. FleetSequencerTest is UNMODIFIED by this diff (staged files are backlog.md, SPEC.md, and the new file only) and its 15 @Test methods do not include it. The same wrong class-qualified name is in backlog.md:42's done cell, twice over -- it also says the mutation "fails the new test alone out of `FleetSequencerTest`'s 16", and FleetSequencerTest has 15 tests, not 16. The 15+1=16 arithmetic is the tell: both documents were written against a plan to put the test IN FleetSequencerTest, the split to FleetSequencerCostTest happened afterwards, and neither document was updated. Failure scenario: the task's whole deliverable is "price commit forwarding in ONE PLACE and pin the count". A reader arriving at the SPEC cost row to verify the +3 greps FleetSequencerTest, finds nothing, and concludes the pin does not exist -- which is the exact state the row was written to correct (its predecessor claimed "Nothing PINS the per-flush shape"). At M5.6g the same reader is told to change "that assertion" in a file that does not contain it.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader arriving at the SPEC cost row to verify the +3 greps FleetSequencerTest for the named method, finds nothing, and concludes the pin does not exist -- which is exactly the state the row's predecessor described ("Nothing PINS the per-flush shape"). At M5.6g the same reader is instructed to change "that assertion" in a file that does not contain it, and either edits the wrong file or gives up.

findings.summary: `{@link #aFollowerDoesNotWriteTheCHAINItself}` is a same-class reference to a method in FleetSequencerTest, so it resolves to nothing
findings.detail: The class javadoc at :29 gets it right -- "{@code FleetSequencerTest}'s {@code aFollowerDoesNotWriteTheCHAINItself}" -- and the method javadoc at :67 then writes it as `{@link #...}`, which javadoc reads as a member of FleetSequencerCostTest. It is the same leftover as the finding above: correct only if the test had stayed in FleetSequencerTest. javac does not check it and check-links.sh only covers markdown, so nothing catches it. Failure scenario: the PUT-exclusion argument ("it is excluded here so the two assertions cannot mask each other") rests entirely on the reader being able to reach the assertion that does pin the PUT; an IDE or `gradlew javadoc` gives an unresolved reference, and the reader is left unable to confirm the PUT is pinned anywhere. Fix is `{@link FleetSequencerTest#aFollowerDoesNotWriteTheCHAINItself}`.
findings.failure_scenario: The PUT-exclusion argument ("excluded here so the two assertions cannot mask each other") rests on the reader reaching the assertion that does pin the PUT. An IDE or `gradlew javadoc` gives an unresolved reference, so the reader cannot confirm the delta PUT is pinned anywhere and either re-adds a PUT assertion here (the masking the javadoc warns about) or assumes it is unpinned.

findings.summary: "SPLIT FROM FleetSequencerTest WHEN IT CROSSED 700 LINES" states a past event that did not happen -- FleetSequencerTest is untouched at 657 lines
findings.detail: Nothing was moved out of FleetSequencerTest by this diff; it is not in the staged set and `wc -l` gives 657. The split is substantively justified -- the new test adds roughly 70 net lines to a 657-line file, which would breach code-structure.md rule 1 -- but the sentence as written describes a file that crossed the limit and was cut, and DeadPeerTest.java:20 uses the identical formula for a split that genuinely did move content out, so the two read as the same event when only one is. Failure scenario: a reader auditing whether the split was forced or convenient checks FleetSequencerTest's length, gets 657, and concludes the stated reason is false -- discrediting the seam argument the rest of the javadoc rests on. "Split rather than push FleetSequencerTest past 700 lines" is the true claim and is just as strong.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader auditing whether the split was forced or convenient checks FleetSequencerTest's length, gets 657 with no lines removed by this diff, and concludes the stated reason is false -- discrediting the seam argument the rest of the class javadoc rests on, and with it the decision to leave aFollowerDoesNotWriteTheCHAINItself behind.

findings.summary: The M5.6g hand-off names two sites that change ("this cell and that assertion") when at least four do, including the test's own method name
findings.detail: The task asked for the price in ONE place. As landed the 3-request arithmetic is restated in four: ADR-0039 (pre-existing, "one ... down from three"), SPEC.md:305, backlog.md:42's done cell, and FleetSequencerCostTest.java:64-87 -- which spells out the same GET/STAT/GET breakdown and encodes the number in the METHOD NAME, `aForwardedCommitCostsTHREEReadsAtANYNumberOfStreams`. When M5.6g lands, the SPEC's own instruction ("this cell and that assertion both change to 1") undercounts: the cell, both `isEqualTo(3L)` values, the method name, and the javadoc breakdown at :66-70 all change. The two assertion values are self-enforcing (they red), but the method name and the javadoc are not, so the file would sit claiming THREE while asserting 1. Failure scenario: M5.6g lands, the author follows the SPEC's two-site instruction, and the sequencer suite ships a test named ...CostsTHREEReads... asserting one -- the same class of stale-prose defect M5.27, M5.32 and M5.34 each exist to clean up. Either name all the sites in the hand-off, or drop the count from the method name.
findings.failure_scenario: M5.6g lands, its author follows the SPEC's two-site instruction, changes the cell and the two isEqualTo values, and ships a test named aForwardedCommitCostsTHREEReadsAtANYNumberOfStreams asserting 1 with a javadoc still spelling out the GET/STAT/GET breakdown -- the same stale-prose defect M5.27, M5.32 and M5.34 each exist to clean up, recreated by the hand-off note itself.
